title: Return requests
description: Handle returns, exchanges and refund requests.

help.title: About Return requests
help.overview: A return request asks to send goods back, exchange them, or refund a product order. The type is return, exchange, or refund. The status walks pending, approved, rejected, received, completed.

sections.title: The path
sections.body: Approve and reject are the decision. Receive and complete are what happens after a yes. Each step is refused if the request is not in the previous state.
items: Approve and reject are only for a pending request. Both record who resolved it and when, and the customer is told.
On approve you can set a refund amount, and it cannot be more than the value of the lines on the request.
Reject closes the request and does not move stock.
Receive is only for an approved request. Complete is only after it has been received.

sections.title: What receive and complete do to stock and money
sections.body: A refund-only request has nothing to put back on the shelf. A return or an exchange does.
items: On receive, a return or an exchange puts the quantities back on hand in the warehouse each line shipped from, and writes a return movement. A bundle comes back as its components.
A line that never took stock, or whose inventory row is gone, is noted on the order instead of restocked.
Complete pays the agreed amount through the order's refund, for a return or a refund. An exchange does not pay anything back.

sections.title: What the request is attached to
sections.body: The request always points at one order and at specific lines of that order.
items: Each line is an order item, a quantity, and a reason.
The customer note and the admin note stay on the request. The money movement, if any, is the order's refund.
Deleting a request is a soft delete and it can be restored.
